suggestions.title: Decide what happens to the eight superseded builds that are still published next to the live site
suggestions.problem: The live site is not one site. This repository publishes 106 HTML pages, and only 27 of them are the maintained build generated by build.py. The rest are seven earlier or parallel builds (dashboard/, annex-88769516/, session-3740f69d/, research/, s2/, site/, docs/), each with its own homepage, its own near-duplicate comparison of the same three products, and in two cases a visible Amazon price. That has two costs. Search: Google's published policy states the presumption that a page matches the overall quality of its domain, and that a review weighs whether 'the same identical or near-identical content appears on multiple other sites' (S30) — nine copies of the same comparison on one origin gives a crawler no signal about which one is maintained, which is why the canonical tag added in this pass (F45) matters. Compliance: Amazon's Program Policies §2(b) permit price display only when Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the Creators/PA API (S2), so any published copy that shows a price is an exposure the maintained build deliberately avoids.

options.label: A. Keep the parallel builds, but make the canonical build unambiguous
options.what: Keep every older build published for auditability, since several are cited as evidence by later flags, and rely on the canonical tags added this pass plus a clear link from previous-passes.html. Lowest effort, keeps the audit trail intact, and leaves the duplicate-content risk in place.

options.label: B. Demote the superseded builds out of search without deleting them
options.what: Add a noindex robots meta to each annex build's pages, so the evidence stays online and reachable but stops competing with the maintained site. Needs a one-line change in each annex's own generator, so it is a cross-session change and must be logged on the task board rather than made unilaterally. Removes the duplicate-content risk while preserving every citation.

options.label: C. Remove the duplicate pages and keep only their evidence files
options.what: Delete the HTML of the superseded builds and keep the JSON, Markdown and evidence files they produced, repointing flags that link to them at the repository instead of a live page. Cleanest search result, largest change, and it destroys published output that other sessions produced. Needs the owner's explicit decision.

suggestions.recommendation: B, and do it before promoting the site anywhere.
suggestions.why: It resolves the search and price-display exposure in one move, keeps every older build citable as evidence — which several flags depend on — and does not delete another session's published work. suggestions.title: Decide what the AI agent in the brief is allowed to read, before the pipeline is written
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for an AI platform that "automates product research, identifies trending and high-converting products, analyses pricing, reviews, competition, and commission potential". Read against Amazon's IP License, most of the automatic half of that is contractually closed. Section 1 states that Amazon "will not allow any third party to use Program Content to, directly or indirectly, develop or improve large language or multimodal models, machine learning models or related technology". Section 2(e) forbids accessing Creators API, PA API or Data Feeds "for the purpose of aggregating, analyzing, extracting, or repurposing any Product Advertising Content ... or in the direct training or fine-tuning of a machine learning and/or foundational model" without Amazon's express prior written approval. An Amazon listing's title, price, rating and review count are Program Content. An agent that reads Amazon listings to learn what sells is therefore the exact use the licence names; an agent that reads manufacturers' own product pages and owner's manuals is not. This is a constraint on design, and it is cheapest to honour before the pipeline is written.

evidence.label: Associates Program IP License, section 1 - Program Content and large language models
Associates Program IP License, section 2(e) - aggregating, analysing, repurposing, and model training

options.label: A. Build the platform on manufacturer and first-party data only
options.what: Research the manufacturers' own product pages and owner's manuals, keep the verified dataset as the single source of truth, and let the generator write only what that dataset contains. This repository already implements the pattern: build.py refuses to publish an article whose numbers are not in data/products.json, and every value on the site carries the official page it came from. Trend and niche signals then come from your own click and earnings data rather than from Amazon's listings.

options.label: B. Apply for Creators API or PA API and operate inside the API licence
options.what: The APIs are the sanctioned route to Amazon data, and their output may be displayed under sections 2(b) and 6(t) with the required display rules. Credentials are tied to the primary account holder and request volume scales with account sales, so this path depends on Q-05 and Q-03 being answered first.

options.label: C. Ask Amazon for prior written approval to use listing content
options.what: Section 2(e) allows the use with Amazon's express prior written approval. Until that approval exists in writing, any version of option A that reads listing text is the prohibited use.

suggestions.recommendation: A, treating B as the later upgrade rather than the starting point.
suggestions.why: The headline capability in the brief is the part the licence most clearly constrains, and knowing that before the research pipeline is designed costs nothing, while discovering it afterwards costs the pipeline. Option A is not a reduced version of the brief: it is the version of it that is lawful, and this repository already demonstrates that it can be built - the whole site is a working example of manufacturer-sourced, machine-written, claim-checked content.
suggestions.risk_of_not_doing: High. A pipeline built on scraped listing content that later turns out to be the prohibited use means discarding the pipeline, and potentially the account, at the point where the most has been spent.

suggestions.title: Give every published value a refresh date, and let the build report what has gone stale
suggestions.problem: Every published figure on this site carries the date it was read, but nothing tells the owner when it should be read again. The dataset already contains a measured case of drift: Chefman's own review counter moved from 1,302 to 1,305 to 1,307 over three days while the average held at 4.6. The Associates application-review criteria recorded in this repository also include a requirement that site content be recent - a requirement that was carried forward rather than re-read until 2026-11-16 (flag F56), and that has now been confirmed: the criterion is "generally within the last 60 days". What Amazon states is the review-side window, though; it does not state a refresh interval for individual published values, so that schedule is still the owner's to set. A page that is silently three months stale still looks authoritative, and the site has no mechanism to say so.

options.label: B. Automate the re-fetch
options.what: Schedule the same fetches this pass made and rewrite the dataset. It works, but a script that writes into the verified dataset can silently overwrite a human correction, so it needs the same no-inference guard the article gate uses.

options.label: C. Freeze the values as a dated snapshot
options.what: Leave the dataset as it is and treat it as a snapshot. Simplest and safest, but a stale specification is a wrong specification the moment a manufacturer changes it.

suggestions.title: Decide what the research agent is, and declare it in every request
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for an AI-powered platform that automates product research, and Amazon's Program Policies contain a section written for exactly that case: IP License §4, the Agent Terms. Read live on 2026-11-16, they require any agent that touches Program Content to identify itself in every HTTP/HTTPS request as "Agent/[agent name]", to avoid obfuscating that it is an agent, never to complete or circumvent a CAPTCHA, and to answer truthfully when asked whether an interaction is human. Amazon also reserves the right to limit agent access by technical measures. None of this was in the canonical compliance register or the platform blueprint before 2026-11-16, even though the site ships an automation blueprint that proposes automated research against manufacturer and Amazon pages. Two things are still unresolved: whether an ordinary public listing page counts as Program Content (the licence defines Program Content around Creators API, PA API and Data Feeds), and the agent's declared name.

evidence.label: Associates Program IP License §4 (Agents) - read live 2026-11-16
Associates Program Participation Requirements §5 - no Special Links or Program Content used to develop machine-learning models without express prior written approval
Associates Program IP License §1 - no third party may use Program Content to develop or improve large language or multimodal models

options.label: A. Identify as an agent, and keep the research stage off Program Content
options.what: Give the fetcher a fixed User-Agent of the form "Agent/zone1-research", never solve or evade a bot check, and scope the research stage to manufacturer pages and other non-Program-Content sources. This satisfies the Agent Terms whether or not a listing page turns out to be Program Content, and it is the design the site's own compliance posture already implies: it publishes no Program Content today.

options.label: B. Ask Amazon first, then build
options.what: Send one written question to Associates Central support: does an automated fetch of a public amazon.com product page count as accessing Program Content under IP License §4, and is a given Agent/... User-Agent acceptable? Build nothing until the answer arrives. The safest order, and the one that costs the most calendar time.

options.label: C. Leave the research stage manual
options.what: Keep automated fetching for manufacturer pages and the Amazon Associates help pages only - the sources this site actually reads - and do not automate anything against amazon.com listing pages. The Agent Terms then never bind, because no agent touches Program Content.

suggestions.recommendation: A, with B running alongside it, and C as the fallback if Amazon says no. The two questions in Q-21 - what counts as Program Content, and what the agent is called - are both cheap to ask and cheap to answer wrongly, so ask while the design is still cheap.

suggestions.title: Pick a publishing cadence and a kill rule before the next article is written
suggestions.problem: Twenty-four articles in twelve days is a burst, not a cadence, and bursts do not compound. The queue has four proposed topics (TP-16, TP-19, TP-20 and the seasonal slots) and no rule for which one becomes next, so the next pick defaults to whoever is writing.

evidence.label: The topic queue, with its proposed rows
This pass's three additions, each tied to a queue row
Google's spam policies: scaled content abuse is the failure mode of volume-first publishing

options.label: A. One article a week, only if it answers a documented gap
options.what: A ceiling, not a target: a week passes without a post if no topic has an official source to answer it. This is the only cadence this repository's own evidence rule can honour.

options.label: B. Two a month, seasonal dates first
options.what: Black Friday, January gift returns, Prime Day. Fewer pieces, each with a real date window and a scheduled re-read of the sources it quotes.

options.label: C. Let measured queries decide, once Search Console has data
options.what: Zero new articles until the property has 4-8 weeks of query data, then write to the queries that already show the site. Requires the owner action in Q-31.

options.label: D. No cadence; publish when an agent pass has something to add
options.what: Status quo, which is how the queue got four proposed rows with no order.

suggestions.recommendation: A now, switching to C the week the Search Console property has data. Both are honest about the constraint: this site will not publish a sentence it cannot cite.
suggestions.why: Cadence is what turns a set of articles into a publication; the kill rule is what stops cadence becoming volume. Suggested kill rule, pre-committed: after eight weeks on path A or B, if the property shows no impressions growth for the cluster's target queries, stop writing and fix findability instead.
suggestions.risk_of_not_doing: Either the burst decays and nothing is published for a month, or the queue is filled on volume - and volume without a source is the exact pattern the spam policies name.

implementation.note: An explicit operating plan now limits publication to useful source-checked work, at most one new/substantially refreshed guide per fortnight, with weekly source review and a no-duplicate-question rule. It is not a running scheduler.

suggestions.title: Decide whether the shopfront applies to the canonical build only, or to every build on the domain
suggestions.problem: This repository publishes seven parallel builds on one origin, each with its own stylesheet and its own copy of the data. The design work in this pass - product rail, merchandising rows, the sticky bar, the mobile type scale - lands in the root build only. A reader who arrives at s2/, dashboard/, research/, docs/ or an annex sees the old look, and no amount of polish on the root build changes that.

evidence.label: The catalogue of parallel builds kept in this repo
Flag F20 (one site, one index) and suggestion SG-05
Google on site structure and canonical URLs for one site

options.label: A. Declare the root build canonical; annexes keep their own look and are no-indexed
options.what: Search engines get one site, readers get one brand, and the verification annexes stay publicly readable as evidence with a visible banner naming them as archives. Cheapest option that ends the two-looks problem.

options.label: B. Port the design system into every build
options.what: Uniform, and it means editing five generators that each have their own reproducibility gate - the work multiplies every time the tokens change.

options.label: C. Move the annexes out of the published site entirely
options.what: Keep them in the repository, serve only the buying guide. Cleanest for indexing, and it removes the reader-facing evidence trail the brief asked to keep published.

suggestions.recommendation: A. It is the only option that makes 'the site' a single thing to design, without destroying the audit trail that is this project's actual differentiator.
suggestions.why: Every design decision made from now on has to answer this question first, or it is made seven times. That is why it sits above the visual work, not beside it.
suggestions.risk_of_not_doing: Polish decays at the edges of the domain, and a crawler or a reader with a search-result bookmark keeps finding the older, less trustworthy-looking version.

suggestions.title: Decide how this site may show social proof at all, given the policy it obeys
suggestions.problem: No Amazon star rating, review count or price appears anywhere on the site, because the program policies restrict how an Associate may display them. The site therefore shows nothing that looks like popularity - which is compliant, and also reads as a wall of tables to a shopper. Manufacturer-hosted ratings are the current compromise: they are the brand's own figures, labelled as such.

evidence.label: Program Policies 2(b) and 6(t) - price, availability and rating display
The article that already explains the rule to readers
Why the Creators/PA API is the only compliant route to Amazon figures

options.label: A. Status quo: brand-hosted ratings, labelled, with the read date
options.what: What ships today on the product pages ('brand-site rating, not Amazon'). It gives the reader a number and tells them whose number it is.

options.label: B. Get Creators/PA API access and serve Amazon data the way the policy intends
options.what: Prices and ratings shown only when the API serves them through your link. Requires the account, credentials and the qualifying-sales threshold - the three things no agent can supply. Until then this row is a plan, not an option.

options.label: C. Replace ratings with verifiable trust signals
options.what: The read date on every figure, the count of official sources behind a claim, and the list of what the documents do not answer. Less persuasive to a browsing shopper, more durable than any rating, and it is the angle this site can actually own.

suggestions.recommendation: C now, A kept as it is, and B the moment credentials exist. The marketing case for this site is not 'we have more reviews than the other list'; it is 'we are the only page that shows its working'.
suggestions.why: Ratings are borrowed credibility that can be taken away by a policy change or a stale read. Provenance is owned.
suggestions.risk_of_not_doing: The site keeps losing the comparison on the other pages' terms - star counts - instead of winning on the one axis no aggregator competes on.

suggestions.title: Make the row-source gate test the link a reader actually sees, not any link in the row
suggestions.problem: The build refuses a table row that cites no official source, which is the strongest guarantee on this site. It is enforced by scanning the row's raw HTML for a href on a registered host — while several register templates render only the first entry of a row's sources or links array in the summary table. Pass 13 met this five times in one hour: Q-30, Q-31, Q-33, D-17 and R-9 each failed the build until a repository link was moved to the front of the array, which fixes the symptom by reordering data rather than by correcting the rule.

Each path is ordered, names what has to be true before it can start, and says plainly what it will not fix. Pick one path, finish it, then pick the next. The grouping is this pass's judgement; the dependencies inside it are not - they are the blocked_by links already recorded on each row.
paths_note: Suggested order: P1, then P3, then P2, then P4. P3 is placed second because the domain and canonical-build decisions are cheap and everything published afterwards inherits them; if you would rather see the site convince a human before it meets a search engine, swap P2 and P3. The order is judgement. The dependencies are not. P5 is independent: it is the reader-facing polish path and can run in parallel with any of the four above.

paths.name: Make it safe to publish
paths.promise: Remove the four things that could make the site wrong or non-compliant the day it goes live.
paths.effort: S (four small steps, roughly an afternoon, mostly reading screens you already have open)
paths.must_be_true_first: Nothing. This path is unblocked, which is why it is first.
paths.delivers: Every product page can name the model it is describing; the tag that earns the commission is confirmed; the account is known to be past the 180-day qualifying-sale threshold before anyone writes for it; and the one feature the brief asked for that Amazon's policies forbid is permanently off the table.
paths.does_not_fix: It changes no word a reader sees. The site will be correct and still unconvincing.
paths.pick_this_if: You intend to point a real domain at this within the month.
paths.why_first: SG-01 and SG-02 are the two rows that gate other rows (SG-06, SG-08, SG-10). Every path below assumes the product identity is settled, because content written against the wrong spec table has to be rewritten, not edited.

paths.name: Make it read like a shop, not an audit
paths.promise: Turn a careful source register into a page a buyer can act on.
paths.effort: M (a day or two of writing and one round of design)
paths.must_be_true_first: Path 1, or at least SG-01 - the landing page cannot be rebuilt around a buyer's question while the answer to 'which model is this?' is still blank.
paths.delivers: A landing page that opens with the reader's decision instead of the project's provenance; a named author and an honest method line; the eight existing articles given one job each instead of overlapping; the two facts a buyer actually asks for added to each product page; and a visual layer, licensed before it is published rather than after.
paths.does_not_fix: Traffic. A better page with no visitors is still a page with no visitors.
paths.pick_this_if: The site already gets some visitors, or you are about to send it to someone.
paths.why_first: Conversion work on an unverified product table converts the wrong product.

paths.name: Make it findable
paths.promise: Give search engines one site to index and a reason to rank it.
paths.effort: M (a decision about the domain, then mechanical work)
paths.must_be_true_first: A decision on Q-07 (one site, one domain) and, for SG-10, an answer to Q-11.
paths.delivers: One canonical site instead of eight parallel builds competing with each other; a domain you control rather than a GitHub Pages subpath; the article cluster pointed at distinct search intents; and the commission rate stated where the category is genuinely knowable.
paths.does_not_fix: Whether the content is worth ranking. It removes the structural reasons it cannot.
paths.pick_this_if: You want organic search traffic, which is the only traffic this model gets for free.
paths.why_first: Eight parallel builds on one domain is the single largest reason a search engine would treat this site as low quality, and it is fixable in an afternoon once the decision is made.

paths.name: Make the machinery trustworthy
paths.promise: Automate the parts that can be automated, and put a gate in front of the parts that cannot.
paths.must_be_true_first: Path 1 for SG-06 (it depends on whether Creators API access exists - Q-05), and Q-08 for SG-08.
paths.delivers: Automated drafting kept, with a claim-check gate as the thing you trust rather than the draft; click and conversion measurement that does not breach the privacy disclosure; a flag register where a row number means one thing; a public corrections log; and a settled position on which catalogue data the site may show.
paths.does_not_fix: Revenue on its own - it makes the other three paths repeatable instead of one-off.
paths.pick_this_if: You plan to add products beyond these three, at which point doing this by hand stops working.
paths.why_first: SG-07 already forbids one automation the brief asked for (price tracking). Automating before the guardrails exist automates the mistakes too.

paths.name: Make it read like a publication
paths.promise: The reader-facing polish path: authorship, navigation, brand, imagery, seasons, and clusters - the changes that make the site feel published rather than generated. It carries the parallel passes rows too (SG-27..SG-30: nav labels, the shipped RSS feed, Search Console, reader capture).
paths.effort: M (mostly small changes in the generator and the nav; the calendar and brand rows need one owner decision each)
paths.must_be_true_first: P1's safety rows (SG-01, SG-02, SG-07, SG-11) should be settled, because polish on top of an unconfirmed product identity polishes the wrong thing. Nothing else blocks this path.
paths.delivers: A site a reader can trust at a glance (bylines, one brand, a shopping-shaped nav), a seasonal content rhythm that ships before the moment, a cluster map the generator maintains, and an automation plan pointed at a live API. P5 now also carries the parallel pass's rows (SG-23..SG-25: imagery licensing, seasonal shipping, one compliant call-to-action). These are exactly the changes the brief's 'polished marketing affiliate website, not AI slop' ask describes.
paths.does_not_fix: It does not settle product identity (Q-01/Q-02), the Associates tag (Q-04), or the domain (Q-07) - those remain owner decisions the polish cannot make.
paths.pick_this_if: You want the site to win readers while the account questions are still open, and you are willing to answer two one-message questions (Q-25 brand, Q-23 publishing decisions) to unblock it.
paths.why_first: Not first - parallel. Unlike P1, nothing here can make the site wrong; it can only make it more or less convincing. It can run alongside any other path.

paths.name: Make the money path real: five links, one tag, one report row
paths.promise: Turn what the owner supplied on 2026-11-17 — two more links and a tracking ID — into a site whose commercial links are attributed on evidence rather than on assumption, and whose product set is a decision instead of an accident.
paths.effort: S (two of the three rows are a browser, a report and five minutes; the third is a reading-and-choosing task)
paths.must_be_true_first: Nothing outside the owner's screens. The intent register, the link-test fields, the tagging contract and the five event definitions are merged and enforced by the build, so this path answers questions rather than waiting on code.
paths.delivers: Every submitted link confirmed or explicitly parked; a tracking ID whose attribution has been observed in the Tracking ID Summary Report rather than inferred from markup; a per-channel sub-tag scheme that needs no infrastructure; and a measurement layer whose status, service and disclosure say the same thing in the same tense.
paths.does_not_fix: It will not produce a conversion figure. Orders come from an authorized first-party report, and the campaign ledger's first row is transcribed by a human or does not exist.
paths.pick_this_if: You intend to earn from this site rather than merely publish it.
paths.why_first: It is the only path where the owner's own action unblocks the largest number of other rows, and the only one whose entire bottleneck is a login this repository will never have.

paths.name: Make the shop look bought-in
paths.promise: The presentation layer a buyer judges the site by: products before process, a decision block on every product page, a mobile route that survives scrolling, and the two things that have to be decided by a human before the look can finish - photography and hosting.
paths.effort: Three quarters of it shipped on 2026-11-17 (SG-39, SG-40, SG-41, and SG-44/SG-45/SG-47 as decisions). What is left is two owner actions: the photography route (SG-42) and the measurement host (SG-47).
paths.must_be_true_first: You accept that no picture, no price guarantee and no popularity claim appears on this site unless its source is on the page. That is the constraint the design has to live inside; it is why SG-42 is the highest-leverage row in the path.
paths.delivers: A front page that opens with goods, product pages that answer the two buyer questions in order, a mobile reader who is never stuck, and a design record an owner can review without reading the build.
paths.does_not_fix: Traffic, indexing of the parallel builds, and the fact that the site cannot yet see a single click. SG-44, SG-47 and Q-31 are the rows that fix those.
paths.pick_this_if: You want the site to look like a publication someone runs, and you will supply one of the two decisions.
paths.why_first: It sits last in the order on purpose: the compliance floor (P1) and findability (P3) are what make a polished page worth polishing. If you want the visual change before the indexing work, put P7 ahead of P3 - nothing in P7 depends on P3, and nothing in P3 depends on it.
